deviations.edit: ClickHouse 25.8 dialect workaround. Aliasing an aggregate output with the SAME name as its source column (min(is_staged) AS is_staged, alongside argMin(hotlist_id, (toUInt8(is_staged), hotlist_id)) in the same SELECT) throws Code 184 ILLEGAL_AGGREGATION — the analyzer substitutes the alias definition back into sibling expressions in the same scope. Worker isolated it with a minimal numbers() repro against the local container. Fix: the address_hour CTE's own output aliases are out_hotlist_id / out_is_staged instead of hotlist_id / is_staged. The aggregate EXPRESSIONS are byte-for-byte unchanged; only CTE-local alias names differ. Final projected column names, ordering, and the PHP return mapping are unchanged.

The 0.27% RATIO survives (view-weighted, and check-ins are generated per-org-view, so it is the right basis for the per-bucket decision), but the absolute counts and the 1.52x fan-out must not be quoted as fleet-wide. The AC-4 conclusion drawn from 1.52x is withdrawn; the honest range is ~1.0-1.4.
